title: The Elfin Hill

full_text:
A commotion stirred through the enchanted forest! Several giant lizards scurried across the hollow oak roots, whispering that the Elfin Hill was to be raised on four glowing pillars that very night to host a grand banquet for royal guests from Norway.

The old Elfin King's house was swept with rush-brooms and polished until the mica stones sparkled like diamonds. The kitchen roasted fat earthworms, spiced frog-legs, and brewed sweet mushroom mead. The King of the Dovre Mountains in Norway had arrived with his two wild, boisterous sons to seek brides among the Elfin King's seven lovely daughters.

The old Norwegian Troll King sat on the seat of honor, telling grand sagas of roaring waterfalls, pine-clad fjords, and granite crags until his eyes sparkled. His two sons, however, were ill-mannered louts: they threw roasted beetles on the polished floor, put their muddy boots on the table, and fell asleep snoring.

The seven elfin maidens demonstrated their accomplishments: the first could turn mist into silver silk; the second could play the harp so sweetly that the trees wept sap; the third could brew magical potions; the fourth carried poetry in her fingers. But the Norwegian Troll King dismissed them all until he came to the youngest daughter.

She could tell enchanting tales of every stone, leaf, and mountain spring in the world.

"You shall be my queen!" roared the delighted old Norwegian Troll King, ignoring his lazy sons entirely. "You shall sit upon my throne of granite and tell me stories through the long winter nights!"

And as the cock crowed at dawn, the pillars sank back into the earth, the hill closed its grassy dome, and the boisterous sons hurried back to their snowy crags, while the wise maiden found an enduring kingdom in the northern mountains.
moral: Pretentious vanity and pompous matchmaking often reveal the shallow nature of worldly pride.
